chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic
And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to undertake the journey to it.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the ability (sabil)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That there be for him what he can perform Hajj with.'

I said: 'What about the one who is offered that, from which he can perform Hajj with, but he is too embarrassed from that? Is he from the ones who has the capacity to journey to it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. What is his matter that he is too embarrassed?'
And even if he has to perform Hajj upon an amputated tailless donkey? So if he is able to walk part of the way and ride part of the way, let him perform Hajj.

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: Ability or capacity to undertake the journey

ai.seo_question: What constitutes 'ability' (istita'ah) for the obligatory Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expands the definition of 'istita'ah' (ability) beyond mere financial sufficiency to include the practical capacity to complete the journey, emphasizing that modesty should not hinder the obligation. The hadith illustrates this flexibility by noting that even relying on a simple, imperfect beast of burden or combining walking and riding satisfies the condition, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that ease is granted within the bounds of genuine capability. This interpretation aligns with the principle of 'la haraj' (no difficulty) in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring the duty remains accessible to those with varying degrees of resources.
